nodes.label: AMPM Developer Technical Specification v1.0 (20 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: One coherent starting specification for AMPM's connected wedding platform covering functional scope, screen flows, data model, permissions and acceptance criteria; subscription prices, service fees, legal terms, integrations and final visual design remain decisions for AMPM.

nodes.label: Product Definition — connected wedding-planning and management platform from enquiry and paid hotel discovery through consultancy, planning, guest management, execution and closure (not merely a public hotel or vendor directory)
Four Connected Experiences with Access Rules (public website, client portal, AMPM team workspace, guest RSVP portal)
Public Website (explain AMPM, showcase approved work, capture enquiries, explain demo/subscription; public pages only, no unrestricted private database access)
Client Portal (hotel discovery for subscribers; wedding workspace for engaged clients; access depends on subscription, service agreement and project permissions)
AMPM Team Workspace (leads, hotels, projects, vendors, budgets, guests, approvals, execution; role-based and project-scoped access)
Guest RSVP Portal (wedding-specific access; no viewing other guests' private records)

Business Journey (lead -> controlled demo -> subscription after payment -> destination/hotel discovery -> optional consultancy -> scope/fees/agreement and wedding project -> parallel planning -> 5-10 vendor options per category -> execution, departures, closure)
Critical Rule — Hotel-Discovery Subscription Does Not Automatically Activate Full Wedding Management
nodes.rationale: Clients may select only the services they want; hotel discovery, optional hotel consultancy and complete wedding management are distinct but connected service stages.

nodes.label: Public Website Screen Map (Home, How it works, Destinations/selected work, Services, Enquiry form, Demo/subscription)
Enquiry Form (name, contact, contact preference, tentative dates/destination, guest estimate, source/consent -> lead record in CRM)

Client Portal — Hotel Discovery Screens (sign-in/activation, subscriber home, destinations, hotel search/filter, hotel detail with last-verified commercial information, compare and save, request assistance, track enquiry/negotiation/visit/proposal/booking status)

Client Portal — Engaged Wedding Client Screens (dashboard, overview and decision-maker contacts, functions, client-facing budget, vendor options, design studio, invitations/save-the-dates, RSVP progress, menus, documents and notifications)
Team Workspace Areas (Home, Leads/Clients, Hotels, Weddings, Guests, Vendors, Tasks/Operations, Finance/Reports, Settings)

Guest RSVP Flow (wedding-specific link; contact details and family group; respond for accompanying family; per-function attendance; travel/accommodation if requested; confirmation; AMPM RSVP team records call-assisted responses in the same database)
nodes.rationale: Privacy: do not require Aadhaar/passport uploads for every guest by default; collect identity documents only for a defined necessary use case, conditionally and with restricted access.

nodes.label: Module Inventory (14 modules with core records and outcomes)
Module: CRM / Subscriptions (lead, contact, account, subscription, payment, service agreement -> lead conversion and access control)
Module: Hotel Intelligence (destination, hotel, room category, inventory snapshot, venue, media, verification -> curated discovery with freshness labels)
Module: Hotel Consultancy (availability enquiry, response, negotiation, site visit, proposal, booking milestone -> traceable hotel assistance)
Module: Wedding Project (project, client contacts, scope, team assignment -> single source of truth per wedding)
Module: Budget / Finance (budget category/line, quote, contract, invoice, payment, cost entry -> estimate, approval, actuals, variance)
Module: Functions (function, schedule, checklist, venue, run-of-show -> function-level plans connected to the wedding)
Module: Creative / Approvals (design brief, version, comment, approval, change request -> versioned creative decisions)
Module: Vendors (vendor, category, portfolio, proposal, assignment, scope, contract -> curated options and delivery tracking)
Module: Invitations / RSVP (invitation, recipient, guest, family group, response, attendance -> invitation-to-attendance workflow)
Module: Rooms / Logistics / Hospitality (room allocation, travel segment, transfer, vehicle, request/ticket -> guest movement and support)
Module: Food / Entertainment / Production (menu version, artist booking, technical rider, production item, readiness check -> function readiness)
Module: Tasks / Risk (task, dependency, staff assignment, incident, resolution -> operational accountability)
Module: Closure (departure record, lost-and-found item, vendor completion, final account -> formal closeout)
Module: Administration (user, role, permission, notification, audit event, configuration -> secure configurable operation)
Suggested Relational Data Model (logical model; relational database for structured records plus secure object storage for media; developer finalises SQL types, indexes, constraints, migrations)
nodes.rationale: Security note: internal cost, margin, private notes and identity-document references must be separately protected or guarded by strict server-side field permissions; never send restricted data to a client and merely hide it in the interface.

nodes.label: Table: users (id, name, email, phone, status; roles and project assignments)

Table: leads (id, source, status, contact, requirements, owner_user_id; can convert to client account)
Table: client_accounts (id, primary_contact_id, status; subscriptions, service agreements, projects)
Table: subscriptions (id, account_id, plan_id, status, starts_at, ends_at; controls hotel-discovery entitlement)
Table: payments (id, account/project_id, purpose, amount, currency, status, provider_ref; subscription/service/vendor payment record)
Table: service_agreements (id, account_id, service_type, scope, fee, terms_version, status; determines service access)

Table: hotel_rooms / venues (id, hotel_id, category/type, capacity, facilities; may be proposed for a wedding)
Table: hotel_verifications (id, hotel_id, field_group, verified_at, source, status; freshness of price/facility information)
Table: hotel_enquiries (id, account/project_id, hotel_id, dates, guest_count, status; responses, visits, proposals, negotiation events)
Table: wedding_projects (id, account_id, dates, destination_id, hotel_id, status; parent for wedding records)
Table: project_members (project_id, user_id, project_role, access_scope; project-specific access)
Table: functions (id, project_id, name, date/time, venue, guest_estimate, status; budget, vendors, design, menu, schedule)
Table: budget_lines (id, project_id, function_id, category_id, estimate, approved_amount, actual_amount; links to quote/contract/invoice/payment)
Table: vendors (id, name, category_id, contact, service_area, status; portfolio, proposals, assignments)
Table: vendor_assignments (id, project_id, function_id, vendor_id, scope, status; links vendor to project/function)

Table: contracts / invoices (id, project_id, assignment_id, amount, due_date, status, document_ref; may link to payments)
Table: design_items / versions (id, project_id, function_id, category, version, file_refs, status; revision and approval history)
Table: approvals (id, record_type/id, version_id, decision, user_id, timestamp; decision tied to exact version)
Table: guests (id, project_id, family_group_id, name, contact, restricted fields; one master guest record per wedding)
Table: guest_function_attendance (guest_id, function_id, status, party_count; attendance per function)
Table: rsvp_responses (id, guest_id, channel, response, submitted_at, captured_by; self-service or AMPM-assisted)
Table: travel_segments / transfers (id, guest/group_id, mode, pickup, destination, time, status; feeds transport planning)
Table: room_allocations (id, project_id, guest/group_id, hotel_id, room_type, dates, status; rooming/check-in/checkout)
Table: menus / versions (id, function_id, version, status, submitted_by; versioned menu and approval)
Table: run_of_show_items (id, function_id, start/end, cue, owner, status, actual_times; live execution timeline)
Table: tasks / incidents (id, project_id, owner, due_at/severity, status, outcome; accountability and response)
Table: documents / media (id, owner_type/id, file_ref, visibility, version, uploader; access follows owning record)
Table: audit_events (id, actor_id, action, entity_type/id, timestamp, metadata; important change history)

Field Specification Pattern (name, type/validation, who edits, client/internal visibility, requiredness by stage, automation and report impact; example fields incl. hotel verification date, vendor decision, approval decision, identity document)
nodes.rationale: Avoid making all fields mandatory at project creation; capture information when relevant.

nodes.label: User Roles and Permissions (Super Admin, Sales/Relationship Manager, Hotel/Destination Team, Wedding Project Manager, Creative/Design Team, Vendor Coordinator, RSVP/Guest Team, Hospitality/Logistics Team, Finance/Accounts, Client/Family Decision-Maker, Guest)

Client vs Internal Visibility (client-facing: hotel profiles, approved proposals, relevant vendor details, designs, menus, invitations, approved budget views, shared documents; internal-only: negotiations, cost/margins, candid vendor ratings, staff notes, risk assessments, draft proposals, other clients' data)
nodes.rationale: Backend APIs and file storage must enforce access; hiding frontend controls is not sufficient.

nodes.label: Statuses and Workflow Rules (lead, subscription, hotel enquiry, wedding project, approval, task, room allocation, function readiness, incident, wedding closure)
Function Readiness Status (not started, in progress, blocked, ready, live, completed; requires the checklist or a documented authorised exception)
Approval Tied to Exact Version (draft, submitted, revision requested, approved, rejected, superseded)
nodes.rationale: Approval locks the exact design/menu/proposal version so later revisions never overwrite an approved decision.

nodes.label: Notifications and Automation (payment activates only the purchased entitlement; stale pricing flagged after configurable age; approval notifications; material-change flags on budgets/contracts/tasks/run-of-show; RSVP changes recalculate attendance; logistics alerts; dashboard exceptions; incident escalation; notification log)

Reports and Exports (lead funnel, subscriptions, hotel shortlist, wedding progress, budget variance, vendor status, RSVP/attendance/rooming manifests, run-of-show readiness, incidents, closure report)
nodes.rationale: Exports must respect permissions; sensitive guest, identity, medical, commercial and finance data must not be included by default.

nodes.label: Technical and Non-Functional Requirements (responsive desktop/tablet/mobile; shared backend with separate experiences; secure role-based project-scoped auth; server-side validation; encryption; private file storage; audit trail; backups; search/bulk operations; media optimisation; configurable commercial rules; duplicate-submission prevention; retention rules; documented integration boundaries)

Recommended Implementation Phases (1 Foundation: website/CRM, accounts/subscriptions, hotel database, search, shortlist, enquiry; 2 Wedding planning; 3 Guest operations; 4 Live execution; 5 Stabilisation)

Acceptance Test Scenarios (15 scenarios: enquiry capture, subscription scope, demo isolation, pricing freshness, private negotiation notes, project permissions, independent functions, vendor shortlist size, version-locked approvals, de-duplicated RSVP, attendance impacts, URL/API/file access control, readiness exceptions, incidents, closure checks)

Decisions AMPM Must Confirm Before Implementation (commercial plans, service catalogue, approvals, financial visibility, hotel data governance, guest communications, identity documents, languages/currency, technology ownership, launch scope)

Deliverables Expected from the Development Team (wireframes, user-flow diagrams, ER diagram and schema/migrations, field matrix, role/permission matrix, architecture and integration plan, milestone schedule and cost, test cases, deployment/backup/handover documentation)
Final Product Instruction
nodes.rationale: Build one connected platform; keep hotel discovery, optional consultancy and complete management as distinct but connected stages; connect creative, budgets, vendors, RSVP, accommodation, transport, hospitality and execution to the same project record; no giant mandatory form; reuse records; allow parallel work; simple client views with detailed staff controls; sign off flows, matrices, wireframes and schema before implementation.
